general.title: Myanmar approves death penalty for violent online scam operators
general.summary:
NAYPYIDAW — Myanmar’s military-backed parliament has approved a law allowing the death penalty for people who detain or violently force victims to work in online scam centres.
Union Parliament Speaker Aung Lin Dwe announced during a live television broadcast on Tuesday that lawmakers had passed the Anti-Online Scam Bill following a joint session of the upper and lower houses in Naypyidaw.
MP Aye…

general.title: ม.เกษตรศาสตร์ จับมือกระบี่ ลุยพัฒนาฐานการศึกษา-วิจัยอันดามัน หนุนเกษตร ประมง ท่องเที่ยว
general.summary:
ม.เกษตรศาสตร์ จับมือกระบี่ ลุยพัฒนาฐานการศึกษา-วิจัยอันดามัน หนุนเกษตร ประมง ท่องเที่ยว
ที่ห้องประชุมราชสีห์ ศาลากลางจังหวัดกระบี่ คณะผู้บริหาร มหาวิทยาลัยเกษตรศาสตร์ นำโดย ผศ.น.สพ.ดร.คงศักดิ์ เที่ยงธรรม รักษาการแทนอธิการบดีมหาวิทยาลัยเกษตรศาสตร์ เข้าร่วมประชุมหารือร่วมกับนายสมศักดิ์ กิตติธรกุล นายกองค์การบริหารส่วนจังหวัดกระบี่ ซึ่งได้รับมอบหมายจากนายอังกูร ศีลาเทวากูล ผู้ว่าราชการจังหวัดกระบี่…

general.title: กกต.เปิดคำวินิจฉัย ทำไม 2 สว.อำนาจเจริญ แม่ค้าขายหมู-พ่อค้าก๋วยเตี๋ยวไก่ คุณสมบัติจึงผ่านฉลุย
general.summary:
กกต.เปิดคำวินิจฉัย ทำไม 2 สว.อำนาจเจริญ แม่ค้าขายหมู-พ่อค้าก๋วยเตี๋ยวไก่ คุณสมบัติจึงผ่านฉลุย นั่งเก้าอี้สว.ได้ หลัง ยิ่งชีพ บอกอยากดูมาก เคยเรียกร้องจากกกต.แต่ไม่ได้รับการตอบรับ
เมื่อวันที่ 29 ก.ค.2569 ผู้สื่อข่าวรายงานว่า จากกรณีนายยิ่งชีพ อัชฌานนท์ ผู้อำนวยการโครงการอินเทอร์เน็ตเพื่อกฎหมายประชาชน (iLaw) เรียกร้องให้นายสมพาน พละศักดิ์ และนางแดง กองมา 2 สว.อำนาจเจริญ เปิดรายละเอียดคำวินิจฉัยกกต.…

general.title: แบโผ “ช้างศึก” ร่วมกลุ่มบี ศึก FIFA ASEAN Cup 2026
general.summary:
"ฟุตบอลทีมชาติไทย" อยู่กลุ่มบี ร่วมสาย เวียดนาม, ปากีสถาน, ฟิลิปปินส์ ศึก FIFA ASEAN Cup 2026

สหพันธ์ฟุตบอลนานาชาติ หรือ ฟีฟ่า แจ้งผลการจับสลากแบ่งสายการแข่งขันฟุตบอล FIFA ASEAN CUP 2026 ที่จะถูกจัดขึ้นเป็นครั้งแรก ออกมาอย่างเป็นทางการ เมื่อวันที่ 27 กรกฎาคม 2569 ที่ผ่านมา

สำหรับการแข่งขันรายการนี้ จะแบ่งออกเป็น 2 ดิวิชั่น โดย ดิวิชั่น 1 จะแข่งขันกันที่ประเทศอินโดนีเซีย และ ดิวิชั่น 2 แข่งขันกั…

general.title: “สว.พิสิษฐ์” อัด “ฝ่ายค้าน” ชี้นำสังคมคดีฮั้ว สว.2 สัปดาห์ติด
general.summary:
"สว.พิสิษฐ์" อัด “ฝ่ายค้าน” ชี้นำสังคม 2 สัปดาห์ติด คดีฮั้ว สว. กดดัน กกต. ท้าเช็ก "ใบเสร็จทางการเมือง" ตกรางวัลผู้ช่วย สว. เข้าข่ายผิด ม.77 แฉอีกฝั่งยังปิดห้อง-ยึดมือถือ ย้อนถามหลักฐานคลิป-ตั๋วบิน ได้มาชอบด้วยกฎหมายหรือไม่ เปืด 5 ประเด็นจัดฉากทำเป็นขบวนการ ดิสเครดิต-เซาะกร่อนสถาบัน

นายพิสิษฐ์ อภิวัฒนาพงศ์ สมาชิกวุฒิสภา (สว.) ในฐานะโฆษกคณะกรรมาธิการวิสามัญกิจการวุฒิสภา ให้สัมภาษณ์ถึงกรณีที่พรรคร…
general.source: สำนักข่าวไอเอ็นเอ็น

general.title: เปิดตัวศูนย์ออกกำลังกาย THE O2 BANGKOK & Sapsiree Badminton Academy
general.summary:
เปิดตัวศูนย์ออกกำลังกาย สปอร์ตและเวลเนสคอมเพล็กซ์แห่งแรกของไทย THE O2 BANGKOK & Sapsiree Badminton Academy ปักหมุดศูนย์กลางสุขภาพและการฟื้นฟูครบวงจร

general.title: ประกันสังคม จะเจ๊ง จริงหรือไม่! พิจารณา พรบ.งบฯ70 ซักถามดุเดือด
general.summary:
ก่อนหน้านี้ เราจะเห็นว่าพรรคประชาชน โดย ส.ส.หลายคน อาทิ เซีย จำปาทอง,สหัสวัต คุ้มคง รวมถึง "ไอซ์-รักชนก ศรีนอก" มีการเคลื่อนไหว เกี่ยวกับการผลักดันสูตรแคร์ และรณรงค์เกี่ยวกับการเลือกตั้งบอร์ดประกันสังคมชุดใหม่ รวมถึงมีการตรวจสอบการใช้งบประมาณของประกันสังคมอย่างต่อเนื่อง

ในการประชุมกรรมาธิการวิสามัญพิจารณาร่าง พ.ร.บ.งบประมาณ 2570 "ประกันสังคม" สัปดาห์ที่ผ่านมา อาจทำให้ ประกันสังคมกลับมาเป็นประเด็…

general.title: เล่าประสบการณ์ ถูกจี้ที่จอร์เจีย หวังเป็นเบาะแสตามหา “ฮลุน โซโล่”
general.summary:

general.title_original: British vlogger launches racist tirade against Thais, then blames AI
general.summary_original:
A British social media personality who has previously attracted news coverage over his behaviour abroad has been filmed delivering a prolonged racist and threatening tirade against Thai people before claiming that parts of the footage were created using artificial intelligence.

Daniel Harper, known online as DannyBoy83, repeatedly insults Thais in the video, uses racist slurs comparing them to animals and makes degrading comments about poverty and sex work in Thailand.

“I hate ’em,”

Harper says, before directing further abuse at Thai people and saying he no longer wants to remain in the country.

He also appears to threaten indiscriminate violence, saying that an encounter with Thai people is “going to go off” because he is going to “smack ’em up”.

The recording ends with Harper insulting Thai eating habits and saying he cannot wait to travel to Brazil.

Khaosod English reviewed several copies of the recording preserved and republished by social media users. They show a continuous rant involving the same speaker, voice and setting, with no visible indications that the footage itself was artificially generated or that the remarks were assembled from separate clips.

The original posts are no longer live on the YouTube and TikTok accounts associated with DannyBoy83, although copies were saved and widely redistributed before they became unavailable.

Crime Asia, which drew widespread attention to the footage, reported that Harper recorded the tirade after an alleged altercation with people he described as the “Thai mafia” at a bar in Bangkok’s Sukhumvit area early Tuesday.

In a subsequent video posted at approximately 21:00 on Tuesday, 28 July, Harper claimed that online trolls had altered some of the footage.
“I never said some of that stuff,” he said.

“The trolls have tweaked it. That’s like AI. That ain’t me.”


His wording appeared to dispute only some of the statements rather than deny that the recording showed him. He also said he had a flight scheduled for the following week.

An apology video was reportedly posted and later removed, although Khaosod English has not obtained a complete independently verified copy.

The racist rant has prompted calls for Thai authorities to investigate. No official police or immigration statement concerning Harper had been issued at the time of publication.

Not his first offence

Harper has previously made headlines in Britain. The Sun reported in late 2025 that the then-42-year-old social media personality was arrested at London’s Heathrow Airport after returning from Brazil.

Kent Police reportedly said he had been arrested on suspicion of assault and criminal damage and later released on bail while inquiries continued. An arrest does not establish guilt, and Khaosod English has found no subsequent public confirmation of the outcome of that investigation.

The Sun described Harper as being from Cranbrook, Kent, and reported that he had built an audience of more than 100,000 followers by documenting partying, drug use and encounters with sex workers during overseas trips.

The latest controversy comes amid heightened scrutiny of foreign visitors behaving abusively in Thailand.

Last week, members of an Italian student tour group apologised after a confrontation with a Thai passenger on a Bangkok BTS train went viral. Police later said anyone who believed they had been insulted could file a complaint, while urging the public to avoid direct confrontation and preserve recordings as evidence.

Harper’s statements could potentially draw scrutiny under provisions of Thailand’s Criminal Code concerning threats or insults, although any decision to investigate or bring charges would rest with Thai authorities and depend on the circumstances in which the video was recorded and published.

general.title_original: Myanmar approves death penalty for violent online scam operators
general.summary_original:
NAYPYIDAW — Myanmar’s military-backed parliament has approved a law allowing the death penalty for people who detain or violently force victims to work in online scam centres.

Union Parliament Speaker Aung Lin Dwe announced during a live television broadcast on Tuesday that lawmakers had passed the Anti-Online Scam Bill following a joint session of the upper and lower houses in Naypyidaw.

MP Aye Chan said the final version retained provisions allowing capital punishment for those who detain victims or use violence to force them to carry out online fraud. Lawmakers made few changes to the draft during discussions between the two chambers.

The draft published in May prescribed prison sentences ranging from 10 years to life, as well as the death penalty, for anyone who uses violence, torture, unlawful detention or cruel treatment to compel another person to commit online scams.

The death penalty must be imposed when such abuse results in a victim’s death, according to the legislation.

People convicted of operating online scam centres or carrying out cryptocurrency-related fraud may also face life imprisonment.

The legislation is the first passed by Myanmar’s new military-backed government, led by President Min Aung Hlaing, as the country faces the rapid expansion of scam compounds during its continuing civil war.

Myanmar has become a major base for Southeast Asia’s online fraud industry, including romance and cryptocurrency investment scams targeting victims around the world.

Although some workers enter the compounds voluntarily, many foreign nationals who have been repatriated say they were lured by fraudulent job offers or trafficked before being detained and forced to carry out scams.

The International Organization for Migration said trafficking into Asian scam centres is rising sharply, with victims from more than 80 countries subjected to threats, violence, sexual abuse and other forms of coercion.

Min Aung Hlaing has pledged to crack down on the industry amid mounting pressure from countries including China and the United States. However, rights groups and analysts have questioned the effectiveness of previous operations, with thousands of people reportedly still trapped in scam compounds near Myanmar’s border with Thailand.

China has also imposed severe punishments on criminal groups connected to Myanmar’s scam industry. In January, Chinese authorities executed 11 members of a crime syndicate linked to compounds in northern Myanmar after they were convicted of offences including fraud, unlawful detention and murder.

general.title_original: Japan quake death toll rises to 13 as rescuers search collapsed mall
general.summary_original:
KUMAMOTO, Japan —  29 July 2026, The death toll from a powerful earthquake in southern Japan has risen to 13 as rescuers continue searching for people trapped beneath collapsed buildings, including a badly damaged Aeon shopping centre.

The magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture on the southwestern island of Kyushu on Tuesday afternoon, damaging buildings, roads and bridges and disrupting electricity and transport services across the region.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi confirmed the death toll on Wednesday morning.

“Even now, there are people waiting to be rescued, and it is a race against time,”

Takaichi said. “We will mobilise all available resources to save and assist as many people as possible.”

Firefighters, police and Japan Self-Defense Forces personnel worked throughout the night, focusing on locations where people were believed to be trapped or had been heard calling for help.

Eight people were pulled from the rubble of the partially collapsed AEON Mall Kumamoto in Kashima town early Wednesday.

Two women in their 20s were confirmed dead, while another person was found in cardiopulmonary arrest. Five others were injured, although their conditions were not considered life-threatening.

About 20 to 30 mall employees were reported missing on Tuesday, according to public broadcaster NHK.

Part of the mall was destroyed by an explosion about an hour after shoppers and employees were evacuated following the initial earthquake. Images showed an exterior wall torn away, exposing the steel structure and scattering debris across the car park.

AEON said the cause of the explosion remained unknown. Authorities are investigating whether it may have been caused by a gas leak.

Seven people were also reported missing after a chimney collapsed at a Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro. Four others at the facility were seriously injured.

Hospitals across the region were treating dozens of patients. One hospital stopped accepting new patients after receiving 86 injured people, while another was unable to operate because of a power outage.

The earthquake left more than 36,000 homes without electricity and caused severe damage to major roads. Rail services, including Kyushu Shinkansen bullet trains, were suspended, while the runway at Aso Kumamoto Airport was closed, forcing airlines to cancel or divert flights.

About 260,000 people were advised to evacuate as aftershocks continued across Kyushu.

The Japan Meteorological Agency warned residents in the worst-affected areas to remain alert for another strong earthquake over the coming week, as well as possible landslides.

Authorities also warned evacuees about the risk of heatstroke, with temperatures in Kumamoto expected to reach about 34 degrees Celsius on Wednesday.

Japan’s Nuclear Regulation Authority said no abnormalities had been detected at nuclear power plants in the region.

Several major manufacturers temporarily halted operations after the earthquake. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Sony and Fujifilm evacuated workers from facilities in the area.

 

TSMC said its Kumamoto plant had not suffered damage and was gradually resuming production. Tokyo Electron suspended work at two local plants, while Honda temporarily stopped production at its motorcycle factory.

The earthquake’s epicentre was about 20 kilometres south of Kumamoto city, which has a population of approximately 700,000.

Kumamoto was also struck by a series of major earthquakes in April 2016 that killed hundreds of people, injured thousands and damaged buildings across the prefecture, including the historic Kumamoto Castle.

general.summary_original:
The family of Thai travel YouTuber “Hlun Solo” said on Wednesday that he has still not been found after losing contact with relatives during a trip to Georgia.

Hlun travelled to Georgia to film travel content and last spoke with his brother on July 13. His family has been unable to reach him since and has appealed for help from relevant authorities.

In an update posted on the Facebook account Klose Mos on July 29, Hlun’s brother asked the public to share only information confirmed by the family or people directly involved in the search.

He urged people not to spread rumours, unverified claims or information without a clear source, warning that false reports could create confusion, disrupt the work of officials and cause further distress to the family.

Anyone with useful information was asked to contact the family or notify authorities directly.
